text:
maria: Heads-up — we're seeing a small spike in client errors after the v2 handshake tighten. Clients sending a keyed header `X-Client-Keyed-Ver: tenant=1;feature=f` get 409s if the key isn't in our allowlist. Is that strict rejection intentional?

sam: It was intentional to avoid silent compatibility issues — v2 opts-in to strict handshake so mismatched clients fail fast. But agreed, 409s for unknown keys is noisy.

kevin: Telemetry: 0.28% of requests in the last 24h hit 409 with that header pattern. Affected tenants: T-88, T-214, T-302 (small burst).

priya: Could we do a lenient fallback: log/warn + route to v1-compatible path when unknown keyed headers present? That preserves fast-fail for strict customers but avoids breaking others.

elle: There's an existing console flag `handshake.lenient_mode` in staging but it's global and toggles routing semantics and quota attribution. Need to confirm cost/accounting effects before flipping prod.

maria: Example header payload: `X-Client-Keyed-Ver: clientA=2;beta=true` — v2 currently returns: 409 + body "unknown keyed version: clientA".

sam: Runtime patch we discussed: add a soft-fail mode that converts unknown-key 409 into a 200 with a telemetry tag and routes to compatibility pipeline. Feature-flaggable per-tenant.

kevin: If we route to compat pipeline we must attribute tokens/quota to the original route (v2) OR the compat route? Current billing backfill prefers the served model id. That will change cost reporting.

priya: Suggestion: keep billing attribution to the requested model but add metadata `compat_fallback=true` in logs so console can surface regression. That way finance sees cost, infra sees fallbacks.

elle: Console UX ask: we should surface a small badge on per-route dashboard showing % compat_fallback in last 7d and allow toggling per-tenant lenient handling (canary cohorts).

maria: Ops question: do we want auto-fallback for canary (5%) only, or open to all by default? My vote: start 5% canary + gradual ramp + opt-in tenant override in Console.

sam: Agreed. Implementation plan: runtime change behind flag `runtime.compat_fallback_mode=canary` with param canary_pct. Default off.

kevin: Telemetry work: I'll add a new metric `handshake.fallback_rate` (labels: tenant_id, route, reason) and a sampled agent log with example headers (PII scrubbed) — sampling at 0.1% by default.

priya: I'll own Console side: add toggle, badge, and a small rollout control for percent canary. Also wire a soft alert if fallback_rate > 0.5% for more than 6h.

elle: One more: ensure quota calculations during fallback don't double-count when we re-route to compat pipeline that does its own counting. We need clear single-source attribution.

sam: Implementation note: runtime will mark `x-runtime-compat=1` header downstream so proxies and billing can check and decide attribution.

ops-bot: deploy-bot scheduled canary rollout to staging cluster at 7160094360 for testing.

deploy-bot: @channel staging deploy completed. Please exercise flagged flow and validate metrics.

maria: Next steps: sam PR for runtime soft-fail, kevin adds metrics + sampling, priya adds console toggle + badge, elle to confirm quota attribution plan. We'll reconvene after staging canary. :thumbsup:

sam: I'll open the runtime PR now and link it here.

kevin: Filed infra ticket INF-4021 for the metric + sampling.

priya: Filed console task DC-1987 for toggle + badge mockups.

elle: I'll draft a short ops runbook for escalation if fallback spikes.

maria: Thanks all — keeping this low-friction is critical for our customers during v2 adoption.
